messages:
tj: Heads up — model inference pods in eastus1 GPU pool are seeing intermittent connection drops and 504s to the frontend. Started ~06:15 UTC, affects ~20% of model-serve replicas. Suspect conntrack/NAT exhaustion.

maria: I pulled node metrics for gpupool-eastus1-*.conntrack_count is spiking up to ~261k and nf_conntrack_max is 262144 on affected nodes. Repro is correlated with large prefetch jobs and short-lived HTTP/TCP flows between sidecars.

metrics-bot: [ALERT] pod_connection_errors high (eastus1 gpupool) — error-rate 18% over 5m, netfilter_conntrack_count near limit on 6 nodes.

lee: Can you paste the conntrack snapshot? Also check ip_local_port_range — ephemeral port exhaustion can look similar.

maria: Dumped a few things:
```
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 261987
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
$ cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
32768	60999
$ conntrack -L | head -n 5
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.240.5.21 dst=10.240.8.12 sport=56012 dport=8080 packets=12 bytes=912 ...
```

anya: Interesting — we recently enabled RoCE (RDMA) for intra-node GPU transfers on that pool. RoCE bypasses TCP in some flows, but the model prefetch and traceroute still use TCP/SNAT. Might be mixing eBPF offload + iptables conntrack interaction.

tj: Observed pattern: many short-lived client->sidecar connections (client->proxy->model) that open many outbound ephemeral ports. SNAT table rows accumulate and don't age before new bursts.

lee: Short-term mitigation options:
- increase nf_conntrack_max (sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288)
- raise ip_local_port_range to 1024 65535 to get more ephemeral ports
- reduce conntrack timeouts for TCP_ESTABLISHED: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120

maria: Trying increase on one node now to test. Running: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288 && sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=120

ops-bot: deploy:patch:conntrack-tune — started on node gpupool-eastus1-07 by maria.

metrics-bot: conntrack_count on gpupool-eastus1-07 fell from 261k -> 78k within 30s after patch. Error-rate on that node dropped to baseline.

tj: Good signal. We should still treat that as mitigation, not final. A few follow-ups:
- why so many short TCP flows? investigate client retry/backoff and prefetch batching
- look at kube-proxy/iptables churn vs Cilium conntrack offload behavior
- confirm RDMA/MTU mismatches causing fragmentation or extra control flows

anya: Also worth checking net.ipv4.ip_forward and sysctl net.core.rmem_max/wmem; RDMA MTU 9000 mismatches can produce odd symmetric routing and cause extra SNATs if flows leave node and return via different path.

maria: Found one waveform: many ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT short queues (~20k) likely from client sidecars opening new connections instead of reusing keepalives. Will file ticket to enforce connection pooling in model-serve sidecar.

lee: Long-term fixes to propose:
- implement persistent HTTP/2 or gRPC connection pooling in sidecars to reduce ephemeral churn
- enable conntrack hashing/buckets increase via nf_conntrack_buckets tuned to memory
- consider eBPF conntrack offload (Cilium with ct-map) for high-throughput east-west flows
- schedule heavy prefetch jobs with staggered start to avoid bursts

tj: Ops checklist for rollout:
1) Roll conntrack_max bump to all affected nodes with memory check
2) Adjust ip_local_port_range clusterwide after testing
3) Add regression alert: conntrack_count > 80% for >2m triggers autosuppress/mitigation runbook
4) Engineering ticket to reduce connection churn in sidecars + add permanent keepalive

maria: I'll create the rollout PR and a runbook entry. Also adding a note to the private infra doc about RDMA + conntrack interactions.

anya: One caveat — increasing nf_conntrack_max uses kernel memory; double-check kernel vm and node memory before blanket increase. We should script a graceful ramp.

tj: Thanks all. For immediate visibility I'm pinning the affected node list in the incident tracker and will follow up with root cause once we confirm pooling fixes reduce churn. :thumbsup:
